images.title: Four ways to pay 12 rupees
images.purpose: Show every way to pay an exact amount from a purse with a limited number of coins, laid out as coins on a mat, one kind of coin at a time.
images.composition: A coin mat with four rows of rupee coins of ₹5, ₹2 and ₹1, each row a way to pay ₹12, with the purse under it.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. A coin mat with four ways to pay 12 rupees. The title Ways to pay ₹12 in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (56 px) is centred at x 728, y 60. THE MAT is a rounded rectangle x 100 to 1356, y 110 to 690, filled pale green #D5ECE3 and outlined green #009E73 4 px. It holds 4 rows, each row centred at y 182, 327, 472 and 617. At the left of each row a rounded tag (160 by 70 px, x 130 to 290, white fill, outlined dark #2B2B2B 3 px) with the words Way 1, Way 2, Way 3 and Way 4 in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (40 px). The COINS of a row are circles outlined dark #2B2B2B 3 px, placed left to right with their centres at x 395, 525, 655, 785, 915 and 1045 (only as many as the row needs): a ₹5 coin is 110 px across, filled amber #E69F00, with ₹5 in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px); a ₹2 coin is 96 px across, filled teal #0072B2, with ₹2 in white bold sans-serif (44 px); a ₹1 coin is 82 px across, filled pale grey #D9D9D9, with ₹1 in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (40 px). The coins of the rows, left to right: row 1: ₹5, ₹5, ₹2; row 2: ₹5, ₹5, ₹1, ₹1; row 3: ₹5, ₹2, ₹2, ₹2, ₹1; row 4: ₹5, ₹2, ₹2, ₹1, ₹1, ₹1. At the right end of each row, centred at x 1250, the text = ₹12 in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (56 px). Under the mat, centred at x 728, y 745, the caption In the purse: 2 coins of ₹5, 3 coins of ₹2 and 4 coins of ₹1 in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (40 px). No other text. Nothing else in the frame.
labels: In the purse: 2 coins of ₹5, 3 coins of ₹2 and 4 coins of ₹1

images.takeaway: Going through the coins of the biggest kind first lists every way: here there are 4.
images.context: Concept image for Paying an Exact Amount with Coins, using the example's own purse (practice values). Only the coin values the book uses are drawn: ₹1, ₹2 and ₹5.
images.teaching_notes: Check that each row adds to 12. The slip to watch: stopping after the first way found.

image_decisions.why: The coin mat is the organised list that makes sure no way is missed, and it uses only the coins the book uses.
